text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to play for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid in the Spanish first division game at Camp Nou on Saturday:

Carlos Busquets, goalkeeper, age 29. With Vitor Baia away on international duty, Busquets should get a rare chance to prove himself. Heavily criticised for not using his hands enough, Busquets is frequently likened to a handball keeper.
Julen Lopetegui, goalkeeper, 30. Lopetegui is a former Spanish international but has struggled since signing from Logrones in 1994 and has only an outside chance of making the starting line-up.

Albert Ferrer, defender, 26. Set to make his first appearance since injury cut short his Euro 96 plans at the end of last season. Ferrer makes up for a lack of physical presence with a terrier-like determination in moves down the right.
Abelardo Fernandez, defender, 26. An experienced Spanish international, Abelardo has hardly played this season because of the wealth of central defenders in the Barcelona line-up.
Laurent Blanc, defender, 30. Blanc was one of Johan Cruyff's last signings but has struggled to impress Bobby Robson. May fill the gap left by Miguel Angel Nadal, who is suspended.
Sergi Barjuan, defender, 24. A key factor on the left in both defence and attack, Sergi is one of the quickest men in the Spanish game and an instant first choice.

Gheorghe Popescu, defender/midfielder, 29. Former Spurs man who has been handed the captaincy of the Barcelona side in the absence of Jose Maria Bakero. His previously excellent penalty-taking has become suspect in the past few months.

Luis Enrique Martinez, defender/midfielder, 26. A genuine utility player who pops up in every position except goalkeeper. He has blossomed, primarily as an overlapping full-back, since signing from Real Madrid in the close-season but Robson could move him up to take Luis Figo's place on the wing.
Josep Guardiola, midfielder, 25. Classy and intelligent, Guardiola has returned to favour under Robson after being sidelined by Cruyff.

Ivan de la Pena, midfielder, 20. The shaven-headed darling of the Camp Nou crowd is one of the best passers and set-piece men in the Spanish game. But a desire to do too much every time and an apparent reluctance to tackle back have cost him a regular place under both Cruyff and Robson.
Guillermo Amor, midfielder, 28. Came good at the end of last season with a series of crucial goals which earned him a Euro 96 slot but has hardly played under Robson.
Roger Garcia, midfielder, 19. A possible replacement for Portuguese international winger Luis Figo but has been left on the sidelines after playing regularly under Cruyff.

Giovanni, midfielder/striker, 24. Traded Pele's number 10 shirt at Santos for the playmaker role at Barcelona. A fine finisher and a particularly good header of the ball, Giovanni is the ideal foil for compatriot Ronaldo.

Ronaldo, striker, 20. A series of sensational individual goals has made Ronaldo the undisputed king of the Spanish game and has already gone a long way to justifying the then world record $20 million paid to PSV Eindhoven in the close season.

Juan Pizzi, striker 28. A naturalised Argentine who was Spain's top scorer while at Tenerife last season, Pizzi has been left in the shadow of Ronaldo since joining Barcelona. Tends to squander easy chances.

Hristo Stoichkov, striker, 30. Fiery Bulgarian international who is losing speed and touch with age and has failed to live up to expectations since rejoining Barcelona from Parma in the close-season. Missed Monday's game at Sporting Gijon through injury and is doubtful for Saturday.
